podcast.body: Released in September 1996, this album marked a significant shift with a new, younger lineup including guitarist Richard Oakes and keyboardist Neil Codling, the band's first ever keyboardist, bringing fresh and agile ideas. While perhaps less profound than *Dog Man Star*, Brett Anderson had achieved his artistic goals with the previous album and sought something fresher. The album masterfully blended Britpop with classic glam elements reminiscent of David Bowie, featuring hit songs like "Filmstar" and "Beautiful Ones." It achieved immense commercial success, selling "like crazy," and is recognized as "one of the great masterpieces of the Britpop movement," arriving somewhat later in the era. "es una de las grandes obras, maestra es el movimiento Britpop."

Suede was one of the "great players" of Britpop. This album, which was anticipated as "el combinam", was released shortly after the main wave of Britpop players emerged. "luego también teníamos a Sui que poco más tardé sacaría el combinam"
